summary: Standards (kept by the brief, so not a defect of this change): split_argv still differs from a POSIX shell in two places the tests do not pin. (1) c.is_whitespace() splits on Unicode and CR whitespace (U+00A0, U+2003, CR) where a shell's IFS is space, tab, newline; quote() always quotes such a word, so the round trip holds, but a hand-written command with an unquoted NBSP splits differently from sh. (2) inside double quotes only the escaped quote and escaped backslash are read, while sh also reads backslash-dollar, backslash-backtick and backslash-newline there; the brief and contract 7.1 say 'as before'. quote() never writes double quotes, so no word of quote's is affected. Blast radius: a tool whose command uses backslash-dollar inside double quotes would be reported by L0.next although a shell runs it as written.
